includes: Outer journal ACK timing from commit 594b99a7; retains inner native-child and parent spans separately.
target: The serial protected journal service allocated a fresh maximum-size response array for every ACK. Reuse one zeroed response buffer for the lifetime of serve instead.
ownership: One buffer per serial connection, no shared global pool. io.Writer owns bytes only during Write. The service immediately exits on a failed/short write, so it never reuses a buffer after uncertain native I/O. The ordinary stateless helper remains for other callers.
invariants: Clear the entire array before each encode. Preserve private cursor/desktop fields, failure certainty, framing, sequence order, one Write, original write errors, short-write handling, authority checks and deadlines. No input retry or asynchronous successful ACK.

benchmark.scope: One response encode and io.Discard.Write. Same new codec, fresh-array helper versus connection-owned buffer. Excludes real pipes, new service timing allocations, native input, CPU saturation and GC pause behavior. Not a physical handoff benchmark or a whole-system allocation comparison.

quantitativeEffect: For this serialization site only, 1000 ACK/s removes 1000 transient allocations and 144000 allocated bytes/s. The connection buffer is allocated once. Does not establish that GC frequency or the prior 1.47s wait is fixed.
validation: Five related package suites and vet passed for outer timing; full inputworker suite and vet rerun after buffer reuse. Selected outer-service/production-worker/snapshot/buffer tests passed under race detector. Byte-for-byte fresh/reused framing, detailed-to-plain clearing, following-ACK alignment, single attempted short/failed writes verified.
rollout: Build and verify matching local g519 workspace/setup, install on A and B, verify READY and shared connection using CLI, then collect paired diagnostics. Physical latency and reliability remain pending the next user trial.
impact: Only local profiled metadata and response-buffer ownership. No external API, DB, repository hygiene or runner change. No push or public release requested.
